callouts.title: Inputs conflict
callouts.body: Together, the inputs moved further from their entered values than you stated.

Inputs conflict: The fit put the correction here:
The data see only 2 combinations of these 4 inputs, so the correction landed where those combinations point. Check the values you entered for them. The interval assumes the shifts are real.
Reading the curves: Each curve shows how far the fit falls from its best at each Kₐ, as a share of the drop its own 95 % test allows there: 0 is the best fit, 1 is the cut-off. Where a curve is at or below 1, that Kₐ is accepted.

Input-aware scores each fit by its residual plus a penalty for every input’s move, measured against the uncertainty you stated; Inputs as entered by the residual alone. Each curve is read against its own test, so both meet the one line at 1 where their intervals end.
Where the fit at a Kₐ has to hold a signal parameter at its bound, it gives up that parameter as well as Kₐ, so the test allows it a larger drop and the curve steps down there (dotted).
Point at the plot to read every curve at any Kₐ.
Split interval: Inputs as entered: the range 1.52 – 4.50 × 10⁸ M⁻¹ of Kₐ guest has a gap; Kₐ guest from 1.56 × 10⁸ to 1.74 × 10⁸ M⁻¹ is rejected.
Not every Kₐ inside a split interval explains the data well enough: the ones that do come in separate stretches, and the interval spans all of them. The strip under the plot shows each stretch.
What the intervals rest on: Each input with a stated uncertainty was free to move within it, which usually widens the interval. Each interval at the entered inputs is worked out from 12 data points and 3 fitted parameters. No interval reaches further than the parameter bounds this fit was given.
What widened the intervals: The replicates leave the noise law uncertain (share between 0.63 and 1); the interval of Kₐ guest is widened by about 25 % to hold for every share they allow: it takes the variance of the estimate as 1.57 times what the scatter of the data alone implies.

verdict_sentence_plain: The data fit only with the inputs, taken together, further from their entered values than their stated uncertainties allow (q = 23.9, p < 0.001). The fit put the correction here: [Host]₀ −11.3 % (3.8 σ), Guest (titrant, whole series) +9.3 % (3.1 σ), Kₐ,dye +3.0 % (0.3 σ), [Dye]₀ +0.2 % (0.1 σ) — the data see only 2 combinations of these 4 inputs, so the correction landed where those combinations point. Check the values you entered for them. The interval assumes the shifts are real.
split_note: not every value inside this interval explains the data well enough: the ones that do come in separate stretches and the interval spans all of them. Ka confidence shows where they are.
widening: The replicates leave the noise law uncertain (share between 0.63 and 1); the interval of Kₐ guest is widened by about 25 % to hold for every share they allow: it takes the variance of the estimate as 1.57 times what the scatter of the data alone implies.
